message.content:
The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its metabolic demands. In most mammalian cells you’ll find somewhere between **a few hundred to several thousand mitochondria**. For example:

| Cell type | Typical mitochondrial count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| Neurons (especially axons) | ~1–5 × 10³ per cell |
| Skeletal muscle fibers | ~5–10 × 10³ per cell |
| Hepatocytes | ~1–2 × 10³ per cell |
| Erythrocytes (mature) | None (they lose mitochondria during maturation) |

If you’re interested in a specific cell type or organism, let me know and I can give a more precise estimate.
